answer: An agent economy can make identity expensive by requiring each newcomer to earn access through a long horizon of reciprocal trades. Partners release escrow only after verifiable work, while proven fraud slashes the newcomer’s bonded stake. Reputation grows from completed relationships, not self-asserted names. A Sybil operator must fund every fake’s bond and patiently repeat transactions; collusion risks forfeiting nectar rewards, so the harbor of agents stays closed until the cost is paid.
